ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account’s biggest missed volume is in the two non-brand Search campaigns, and it’s primarily rank-constrained rather than budget-constrained. Both non-brand campaigns are only capturing ~1/3 of available impressions (33–35% search IS) while losing ~51% to rank, with moderate budget loss (14–16%) and plenty of budget headroom (only ~61–64% utilization). Keyword evidence reinforces this: several high-quality keywords (QS 7.0–8.5) still have low impression share (30–36%) driven by very high lost-to-rank (64–70%), indicating bids/ad rank are not competitive enough on the most valuable generic terms. Secondarily, there’s efficiency drag from low-intent service-policy queries (QS 4.0–4.5 with very high cost/conv) and a meaningful amount of competitor-brand “zero-click” exposure (10,640 impressions; 48.5% of search-term impressions coming from those terms) that likely contributes spend/auction pressure without returning value.
notable_patterns: Non-brand Search is structurally under-serving demand: Flights has 33% search IS with 51% lost to rank vs only 16% lost to budget, and Hotels & Packages has 35% search IS with 51% lost to rank vs only 14% lost to budget (both with budget utilization only 63.6% and 61.4%).

High-quality generics are still losing auctions on rank: “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) has only 34% IS with 66% lost to rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) is 36% IS with 64% lost to rank; “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) is 30% IS with 70% lost to rank.
Hotels & Packages has a low avg quality score (5.1) despite strong ROAS (11.57), suggesting meaningful upside from QS/ad relevance/landing improvements rather than budget expansion alone.
Query mix includes waste/low intent: “flight booking customer service” (QS 4.0) spent £372.28 at £195.94 per conversion; “hotel cancellation policy” (QS 4.5) spent £279.27 at £116.36 per conversion.

Competitor-brand leakage is large and mostly non-productive: 10,640 competitor-brand zero-click impressions (terms: “skyline journeys”, “coastal getaways”, “horizon holidays”) and only 0.5 conversions shown on a competitor term (“trailmark travel quote”).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is missing the majority of eligible demand due to rank, not budget: only 33% search impression share with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, while budget utilization is only 63.6%. High-QS generics like “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) still show low IS (34%) and heavy lost-to-rank (66%), pointing to insufficient ad rank/bids on priority queries.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase competitiveness on the high-intent generic flight terms (bid/target adjustments and tighter query mapping), while cutting/negating low-intent service queries that are inflating cost/conv (e.g., “flight booking customer service” at £195.94/conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Strong efficiency (ROAS 11.57) but constrained by ad rank and quality: search IS is 35% with 51% lost to rank (vs 14% budget), and the campaign’s avg quality score is low at 5.1. High-intent terms like “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) are still only at 36% IS with 64% lost-to-rank, so improving rank and lifting overall QS should unlock volume while maintaining returns.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize quality score lift (ad/landing relevance and segmentation) and raise bids/targets selectively on top-converting, high-intent package queries to reduce lost-to-rank without relying on more budget.

recommendation_cards.title: Push more auction weight onto high-intent non-brand generics that are losing 64–70% of impressions to rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-brand campaigns are under-delivering mainly due to rank: Flights is 33% search IS with 51% lost to rank (only 16% lost to budget; 63.6% budget utilization) and Hotels & Packages is 35% IS with 51% lost to rank (14% budget loss; 61.4% utilization). At the keyword level, high-QS terms still have very low IS because of rank: “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) is 30% IS with 70% lost-to-rank; “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) is 34% IS with 66% lost-to-rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) is 36% IS with 64% lost-to-rank.
recommended_steps: Identify the top 5–10 high-intent generic keywords/ad groups (including the four shown) and raise bids/targets in controlled increments until lost-to-rank meaningfully falls.
Split these priority generics into tighter ad groups (by destination/holiday type) so bids can be raised where conversion value supports it without inflating the whole campaign.
Monitor auction pressure by query and cap increases where marginal ROAS drops below your non-brand threshold (current ROAS baseline: 9.68 Flights, 11.57 Hotels & Packages).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Lost impression share (rank) on the named priority keywords trending down from ~64–70% toward <50% within 1–2 weeks, while holding non-brand ROAS near current levels (≈9–12).

recommendation_cards.title: Lift quality score in Hotels & Packages (avg QS 5.1) to reduce rank loss without paying purely through bids
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Hotels & Packages has avg quality score 5.1 and is losing 51% of impressions to rank despite only 14% lost to budget (budget utilization 61.4%). Keyword-level relationships also support this lever (QS vs impression share r=0.957; QS vs cost/conv r=-0.883), implying QS improvements should simultaneously unlock more impression share and reduce cost per conversion pressure.
recommended_steps: Restructure Hotels & Packages ad groups so each maps to a single clear intent (e.g., ‘all inclusive’, ‘city breaks’, ‘packages’) with query-aligned headlines and descriptions.
Send top ad groups to the most intent-matched landing pages (packages-to-packages, cancellation/policy queries to support pages only if you choose to serve them) to improve landing relevance signals.
For ad groups with mixed intent, add intent-shaping negatives (e.g., ‘policy’, ‘customer service’) so the remaining traffic aligns with commercial package booking intent.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Hotels & Packages avg QS improving from 5.1 toward 6.0+, alongside search IS rising above 35% and lost-to-rank falling below 51%.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut waste from low-intent service/policy queries that carry QS 4.0–4.5 and very high cost per conversion
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Two highlighted terms are disproportionately inefficient: “flight booking customer service” (QS 4.0) spent £372.28 at £195.94 per conversion, and “hotel cancellation policy” (QS 4.5) spent £279.27 at £116.36 per conversion. These intents are unlikely to scale profitably in acquisition-focused non-brand campaigns and can also depress overall ad relevance signals.
recommended_steps: Add phrase/exact negatives around ‘customer service’, ‘contact number’, ‘phone number’, ‘complaints’, and ‘cancellation policy’ in the non-brand acquisition campaigns (or isolate them into a separate support campaign with strict bids if you must cover them).
Review the last 30–90 days of queries for additional ‘support’ intent patterns and negate in batches by theme.
After negating, reallocate the freed spend to the priority generics that are currently losing 64–70% to rank.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Non-brand cost/conv improvement from the worst pockets (e.g., bring £195.94/conv down materially) while maintaining conversion volume.

recommendation_cards.title: Reduce competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage that makes up 48.5% of competitor-term impressions but shows minimal conversions
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: There are 10,640 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and zero-click competitor terms account for 48.5% of search-term impressions in that subset. Only one competitor term is shown converting at all (“trailmark travel quote” with 0.5 conversions), suggesting most competitor-brand exposure is low-yield and may be inflating auction pressure/costs.
recommended_steps: Add exact/phrase negatives for the competitor brand terms driving zero-click volume (“skyline journeys”, “coastal getaways”, “horizon holidays”) in the non-brand campaigns unless there is a deliberate conquesting goal.
If conquesting is desired, isolate competitor-brand into its own campaign/ad groups with capped bids and conquest-specific messaging so it doesn’t compete with generic non-brand budgets/auctions.
Re-check impression and click distribution after negatives to confirm the volume shifts back to generic intent queries (e.g., ‘flights to spain’, ‘all inclusive holidays’).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Competitor-brand impression share within search terms dropping materially (from the current 48.5% in that subset) without reducing total non-brand conversions.

With a daily budget of GBP 6,200 and only 37.84% impression share, there’s meaningful demand you’re simply not getting the chance to compete for right now.
why_now_bullets: Demand is rising on the same generics you’re already losing on — “flights to spain” is up +51% (index 100 -> 151), so staying rank-constrained means missing a growing pool of high-intent searches.
In-market auction pressure is increasing: UK Search Spend Growth QoQ is 22.0%, which typically pushes bids and makes “wait and see” a costly strategy when rank is already the constraint.
